global: MAJOR (process): the per-shot ledger is still missing, and one fix was silently reverted. All five reviewers found no stages.fixes['round2-shots'], even though film-loop passes ledger: 'round<n>-shots' (film-loop.js:149) and film-shots.js:164-166 has a ledger step. That step is a late, low-effort agent that never ran or wrote nothing. Separately, ch08-s05's fix was measured by legibility at 05:11Z and then overwritten at 05:32Z by a later pass, while the shot stayed 'revised'. Fix: (1) Write the ledger in the workflow script itself, deterministically, with no agent: read film.json, merge stages.fixes[key], write. Throw (fail the stage) if any routed shot id has no outcome. (2) Before an author writes a shot file, compare its mtime/hash with the one read at task start; if it changed, re-read and merge. Never let concurrent or resumed passes write over each other. (3) After the stage, run a mechanical note check: for each routed note, grep the shot source for its key strings (e.g. '2 great halls', 'GARY MARCUS', 'BLEU' must be absent, 'ANTHROPIC ·') and downgrade 'fixed' to 'partial' on a miss. (4) Back-fill 'round2-shots' from the round-3 verdict's carriedOverUnapplied and ledgerAudit, then write 'round3-shots' with the word times checked per id.

summary: Round 3 FAILS the gate, but it is the best round yet (mean 7.42 → 7.83 → 8.04). Weighted scores: accuracy 8.17, depth 8.25, clarity 8.0, story 8.17, visual 7.83, sync 7.83, sound 7.67, curiosity 8.42. To pass, every dimension must reach 8 and the mean must reach 8.5. There are no critical issues. Accuracy, depth, clarity, story and curiosity now clear 8. All five reviewers confirm that the round-2 fairness, Act-3 spine, sound-level and end-card fixes landed. Three dimensions remain below 8. SYNC (7.83): the third round of late payoffs. ch15-s09's flame catches on 'from' (the showrunner confirmed +23.50 on the sheet, about 0.9 s after the foley strike). ch08-s13b lights Hinton after 'him'. ch10-s04 shows one beam on 'every' (confirmed at +4.92). VISUAL (7.83): mannequin puppets, blank card stock and the cyan cabinet. SOUND (7.67): the L1505 re-take carries +3.5 dB of trim and is now the loudest line in the film. The process failure remains the root cause. No round2-shots ledger was written, and ch08-s05's fix was overwritten by a later pass. ch09-s05 (Marcus) and ch10-s12 (BLEU) are unapplied for the third round. Round 4 should make the ledger deterministic with an overwrite guard, fix the four sync payoffs (ch15-s09, ch08-s13b, ch10-s04, ch05-s07), apply the two visual kit rules (cards ink with their paper, a puppet rim/detail pass), and take the trim off L1505. Those changes alone should lift sync, visual and sound past 8. The remaining minor notes are cheap and close the carried-over items.

dimensionNotes.accuracy: Every on-screen and spoken quotation matches its source (0 mismatches across 64), and Act 3 now treats the labs even-handedly, including Anthropic's own $1.5B settlement. It stops short of excellent on small things: 'China is one to three years behind' has no dated source (the record says one or two), and two dissenters, Dreyfus's quote and Marcus in 2018, are spoken of or implied but never cited on screen.
dimensionNotes.depth: Both deep dives are expert-grade: you can check the AlexNet stencil sums and the attention softmax (0.20/0.07/0.53/0.20) by hand. Every era has a named belief, a dissenter and a duration. It loses a little where the film says 'next word' rather than 'word-piece', and where the deep-learning era's 2018 critic is missing from his own era.
dimensionNotes.clarity: The key pictures now land: self-attention lights up a whole hall, and backprop gets a readable blame formula. A few unexplained text cards still clutter it, though. One shows layer sizes like '55 · 27 · 13' (a fix that was later overwritten), and another shows a BLEU score the film never defines.
dimensionNotes.story: The question ledger is unusually well kept: 'who taught it', 'can a fence around chips hold' and the dark lantern are each paid off or deliberately left open. It loses a little because the second big question, 'how far, how fast', never gets its own card, and the final match strike lands a beat late.
dimensionNotes.visual: The paper-cut theatre has strong layered sets and memorable images (the stencil cathedral, the Seoul Go board, the winter-blue city). It is held back by puppets that read as smooth mannequins next to the art reference, by cards that flash blank before their text inks, and by a cyan cabinet that breaks the amber palette.
dimensionNotes.sync: Most beats hit their words, but several key payoffs still arrive late. The final candle catches on 'from' rather than 'new candles' (and after its own match-strike sound). Hinton is lit only after 'it found him'. The transformer's every-word-to-every-word threads appear about a second after 'every'.
dimensionNotes.sound: The score is the film's signature: a candle motif, era-specific orchestration and scored silences. The master is clean (-16 LUFS, every line above 10 dB of margin). One re-take, 'Nobody told it... to plan', now jumps out 5 dB louder than its neighbours, and a few lines (the prologue turn, Hinton's last-word hand-off) are still rushed.
dimensionNotes.curiosity: It keeps you leaning forward. Each era is framed as a case-file question, the dissenters are given real airtime, and it ends on open questions rather than a victory lap. This is the film's strongest dimension.
